To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ARV drugs are the major portion of expenditures for HIV/AIDS care in rural China, and that the costs of treating adverse events are associated with CD4 cell counts.
the mean annual expenditure per patient for ARV medications in rural China was US$2 242, with a mean total cost per patient of US$4 276 in the first year of treatment.
the actual expenditures for the first year of HAART were US$29 703 and US$ 23 031 for treating ADEs and opportunistic infections, respectively, among 276 patients in rural China.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the costs of providing care to patients in rural areas of Yunnan and Shaanxi Provinces, which is representative of China's HIV/AIDS epidemic.
the actual costs of HAART and the factors associated with expenditures.
the costs of providing HIV treatment in rural China.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the actual expenditures of HAART in rural areas of the China's Free Care Program were higher than those of developed countries.
the cost of HIV treatment in the rural areas in China is higher than that in the urban areas.

the actual costs for HIV treatment in rural China is high and the government needs to allocate sufficient financial resources to ensure the sustainability and effectiveness of HIV/AIDS care in rural China.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

CD4 cell counts should be used as a guide for initiating ARV treatment, and that patients who are diagnosed with AIDS should be closely monitored to reduce the incidence of ADEs and opportunistic infections.
CD4 cell counts and the presence of ADEs and/or OIs were associated with the expenditures of HIV treatment in a rural area in China.
the costs of ARV drugs and treatment of adverse reactions should be considered when developing HIV/AIDS treatment programs in rural areas of developing countries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Chinese government should consider a policy of providing ARV drugs and other HIV/AIDS-related care services to HIV-positive patients at a lower CD4 cell count level.
the current national AIDS care policy should be adjusted to provide more support to rural patients, especially those in Mangshi County, Yunnan Province.
it is important to consider CD4 cell count level, ADEs and opportunistic infections when planning the HIV/AIDS treatment program in China.
